nodes.label: Stable Identity and Ownership
nodes.rationale: Stable IDs rather than list indices keep definitions, instances, layers, masks, tracks, selection, and provenance aligned across mutations.

nodes.label: Controlled Project Mutation
nodes.rationale: Validation and all representation updates must finish before change events are published so observers cannot see a partially updated object graph.

nodes.label: Snapshot Integrity
nodes.rationale: Deep-copying mutable arrays and remapping duplicated instance IDs prevents undo, cloning, rollback, and restart handoff from sharing invalid identity or storage.

nodes.label: Deterministic Composition Order
nodes.rationale: Serial and parallel composition paths preserve the same layer, object, and suborder so batching does not change visible output or ownership alignment.

nodes.label: Authoritative Release Source
nodes.rationale: A single synchronized source for version metadata and bilingual release notes prevents the application, manager, and package from publishing conflicting release identities.

nodes.label: Atomic Formal Package Boundary
nodes.rationale: The last successful artifact remains intact until a staged replacement passes every payload, metadata, size, and hash check.

nodes.label: Source Fingerprint Guard
nodes.rationale: Save and publish are refused when authoritative source files changed after load so an editor cannot commit a stale release document.

nodes.label: External Runtime Provisioning
nodes.rationale: Keeping .Runtime external and persistent preserves the replaceable single-EXE update boundary while still supporting machines without compatible .NET 8 runtimes.

nodes.label: Stable Scene Instance Identity
nodes.rationale: Projected composition indices are derived and cannot safely identify editable instances; stable scene-instance IDs and resolved provenance must drive transform writes.

nodes.label: Spatial Transform Convention
nodes.rationale: Drawing, hit testing, handles, and feedback use one transform and projection convention so visible geometry and editable coordinates do not diverge.

nodes.label: Mask Clip Order
nodes.rationale: Mask clips are applied before isolated blend groups while preserving deterministic layer and object order so the intended layer range is clipped consistently.

nodes.label: Spatial Renderer Parity
nodes.rationale: Direct2D and GDI reference passes remain equivalent so target failure still leaves a coherent view with matching visibility, clipping, opacity, projection, and overlays.

nodes.label: Stage State Synchronization
nodes.rationale: Input state, editable model state, transient overlays, camera state, and both render backends must move together so commits and cancellations never leave stale visual or UI state.

nodes.label: Stage Cache Invalidation Contract
nodes.rationale: Target-bound resources are invalidated on target reset and data-bound caches on scene identity or revision changes to prevent stale or invalid rendering resources.

nodes.label: GDI Fallback Contract
nodes.rationale: A coherent emergency GDI path preserves usable presentation when Direct2D fails or cannot be captured reliably.

nodes.label: Transient Preview Contract
nodes.rationale: Preview state remains paired, self-clearing, and outside VectorScene unless it is intended to become editable data, keeping canceled interactions non-destructive.

nodes.label: Composed Owner Selection
nodes.rationale: Scene-instance selection follows composed owner provenance rather than source object indices so nested picks edit the intended root instance.

nodes.label: Coordinate Commit Boundary
nodes.rationale: Pointer coordinates pass through Stage conversion APIs and are quantized only at the established commit boundary to avoid preview-to-model drift.

nodes.label: Timeline Identity and Cel Ownership
nodes.rationale: Track identity, Cel ownership, tween evaluation, editor feedback, and composed playback remain aligned so timeline edits resolve to the intended model content.

nodes.label: Stable Track Selection
nodes.rationale: Timeline selection uses stable track IDs and frame coordinates instead of row indices so target synchronization and layout changes do not retarget edits.

nodes.label: Tween Endpoint Validity
nodes.rationale: Tween spans require valid endpoints and deterministic evaluation, and rejected edits leave no partial state.

nodes.label: Cel Ownership Consistency
nodes.rationale: Frame mutation must keep held exposure and the keyframe that owns local geometry consistent.

nodes.label: Tween Endpoint Compatibility
nodes.rationale: Classic and shape tween spans are valid only when their endpoints are compatible and are recalculated after relevant edits.

nodes.label: Monotone Easing Curve
nodes.rationale: Monotone anchors and stable endpoint values prevent reverse or unstable tween progress.

nodes.label: Logical Timeline Command Batching
nodes.rationale: Related updates are batched so a user command emits one notification and one undo entry.

nodes.label: Shortcut Focus Ownership
nodes.rationale: Canvas shortcuts must defer to timeline editors and numeric controls that own the focused key input.

nodes.label: Smallest Covering Suite Set
nodes.rationale: Validation starts with the smallest set that covers every changed contract and broadens only when failures or cross-domain behavior require it.

nodes.label: Single Validation Owner
nodes.rationale: Serial ownership prevents concurrent builds, benchmarks, rendering, or publishing from invalidating results.

nodes.label: Exact Validation Reporting
nodes.rationale: Acceptance reports record the exact command, exit code, first meaningful failure, and dirty-baseline uncertainty.

nodes.label: Synchronized CLI Mode Updates
nodes.rationale: A new CLI mode must update Program, the validation script, suite documentation, and workflow drift checks together.

nodes.label: Release Validation Exclusivity
nodes.rationale: Formal release validation runs alone so disposable publishing, binaries, and resource checks are not contaminated by concurrent work.

nodes.label: Performance Budget Enforcement
nodes.rationale: Budget booleans become acceptance failures only when performance enforcement is explicitly enabled.

nodes.label: Typed Event Binding
nodes.rationale: Reusable controls own presentation state and expose typed intent while MainForm owns domain mutations.

nodes.label: Continuous Editor Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Start, completion, and cancellation events make one continuous gesture produce one undo entry.

nodes.label: Stable Dense Layout
nodes.rationale: Stable dimensions, bounded labels, and batched layout preserve scanability during frequent state changes.

nodes.label: Guarded Model Binding
nodes.rationale: Detaching old handlers and guarding refresh assignments prevents duplicate subscriptions and feedback loops.

nodes.label: Owner-Draw Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Owner-drawn controls must cover interaction, accessibility, DPI, capture loss, and resource disposal as one lifecycle.

nodes.label: Stage Real HWND Exception
nodes.rationale: StageControl and Direct2D require a real HWND, so DrawToBitmap alone cannot verify their output.

nodes.label: Current Documentation Contract
nodes.rationale: The user guide governs current source behavior while release notes govern their specific historical packages.

nodes.label: Save Version Transaction
nodes.rationale: Validated staged writes and read-back with best-effort rollback keep version metadata and announcements coherent during ordinary failures.

nodes.label: External Change Fingerprint Guard
nodes.rationale: Source hashes reject stale previews or overwrites when version or release-note files changed after the manager opened.

nodes.label: Cooperative Publish Cancellation
nodes.rationale: Cancellation stops before formal commit when possible and never interrupts the final replacement transaction halfway.

nodes.label: Development Launcher Boundary
nodes.rationale: Formal packages are contained in release output and must never replace the repository-root source-development launcher.

nodes.label: Baked Mixing Region Mesh
nodes.rationale: Committed strokes store final ARGB vertex colors and topology rather than gradients or mixing history.

nodes.label: Adaptive Mixing Brush Preview
nodes.rationale: Preview rebuild frequency adapts to the active work-grid size so long strokes remain responsive without changing final colors.

nodes.label: Editable Text and SVG Break Apart
nodes.norm_label: editable text and svg break apart

nodes.label: Topology Edit Stability
nodes.rationale: Continuous edits recapture current topology and avoid resplitting existing shared endpoints.

nodes.label: Drag Interaction Optimization
nodes.rationale: Repeated pointer events at the same quantized curve position skip geometry, overlay, and invalidation work.

nodes.label: Atomic Payload Redeployment
nodes.rationale: The old V2DEngine directory is replaced only after the embedded payload is fully extracted and verified, with rollback on failure.

nodes.label: Software Layer Compositor
nodes.rationale: Frames with non-Normal blending use exact software composition so lower pixels, isolated groups, masks, and blend semantics remain correct.

nodes.label: Selection Topology Materialization
nodes.rationale: Virtual local topology is materialized only when a partial edit requires independent geometry, while the gesture remains one undo step.

nodes.label: Mask Then Blend
nodes.rationale: Mask clipping is evaluated before layer blending and opacity so grouped composition preserves expected semantics.

nodes.label: Scene Instance Reference Model
nodes.rationale: Instances store a source reference plus transform, playback, and appearance state so source edits propagate without copying geometry.

nodes.label: Focus-Aware Shortcuts
nodes.rationale: The same key is dispatched by focus context so canvas commands do not steal text, numeric, or timeline editing input.

nodes.label: Direct2D Overlay Rendering
nodes.rationale: Stable GPU backgrounds and lightweight overlays provide immediate interaction while exact topology remains a CPU commit-stage responsibility.

nodes.label: Sphere-Like Two-Tone Volume
nodes.rationale: The darker crescent against the light gray circular fill makes the upper form read as a shaded rounded volume.
